test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which state has special constitutional provisions to protect its tribal customs and laws under Article 371A?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 371A of the Indian Constitution provides special provisions to the state of **Nagaland** to safeguard its social, cultural, and customary practices.
 
• According to Article 371A, no Act of Parliament related to religious or social practices of Nagas, Naga customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice, or ownership and transfer of land and its resources, will apply to Nagaland unless the state assembly decides to adopt it.
 
• This provision was included in the Constitution to respect the unique traditions and customs of the Naga tribes after Nagaland attained statehood in **1963**.
 
• The state has autonomy in matters related to its internal administration and governance to ensure the preservation of Naga identity and heritage.
 
• It is a significant constitutional safeguard aimed at protecting the rights of tribal communities in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 371:** It contains special provisions for several states in India, including Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh, to address their unique needs and challenges.
 
• **Nagaland Statehood:** Nagaland became the 16th state of India on **1st December 1963**, following the acceptance of its demand for statehood under the 13th Constitutional Amendment.
 
• **Inner Line Permit (ILP):** Nagaland is one of the states where the ILP system is implemented under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation Act, 1873, to regulate the entry of outsiders and protect indigenous communities.
 
• **Naga Tribal Identity:** Nagaland is predominantly inhabited by Naga tribes, and each tribe has its distinct customs, dialects, and traditions, which are safeguarded under Article 371A.
 
• **Autonomy in Land and Resources:** Under Article 371A, the ownership and transfer of land and its resources are subject to Naga customary laws, providing autonomy in resource management to the state.
